title: Active and Creative Kids voucher – Provider exemption and eligibility criteria
summary: This page outlines the specific criteria and requirements for providers seeking exemptions to participate in the Active and Creative Kids voucher program.
who_can_apply: Border towns must be located in an ACT, Victoria, South Australia, or Queensland town that borders NSW, deliver an eligible activity, and be assessed by Service NSW.
Online providers must be based in NSW, deliver an eligible activity online, and provide an activity that cannot be delivered in person.
Schools must not be providing a ‘School Activity’ as defined in the program Terms and Conditions for Registered Providers, and must be required to be a Registered Provider.
Providers must meet specific child safe requirements, including relevant Working with Children Checks and e-Learning modules.
All exemptions are subject to assessment by Service NSW on a case-by-case basis and at its absolute discretion.
what_you_need: Proof of location (for border towns, must be in an ACT, Victoria, South Australia, or Queensland town bordering NSW).
Evidence of delivering an eligible activity.
Compliance with all program Terms and Conditions and Guidelines.
Working with Children Check issued in NSW, Victoria, or South Australia.
Blue Card or Blue Card Business Registration issued in Queensland.
Working with Vulnerable People Check registration issued in the ACT.
Completion of the NSW Office of the Children’s Guardian’s Child Safe e-Learning Module.
Completion of SA child safe e-Learning.
Completion of National Principles for Child Safe Organisations e-Learning.

faqs.q: What are the requirements for a provider to be exempt from the Active and Creative Kids voucher program?
faqs.a: Exemption is assessed by Service NSW on a case-by-case basis and at its absolute discretion, ensuring alignment with the program's purpose and following the Registered Providers Terms and Conditions.

faqs.q: What are the criteria for a border town provider to be eligible for exemption?
faqs.a: The provider must be in an ACT, Victoria, South Australia, or Queensland town bordering NSW, deliver an eligible activity, meet all other requirements, and be assessed by Service NSW.
Yes, an online provider must be based in NSW, deliver an eligible activity online, and provide an activity that cannot be delivered in person, while meeting other specific criteria.

faqs.q: What child safe requirements must I meet?
faqs.a: Requirements include a Working with Children Check (NSW, Victoria, or South Australia), Blue Card (Queensland), Working with Vulnerable People Check (ACT), and completing various child safe e-Learning modules.
